peer_identity.arc_label: Princess Oda Capricious as an independent agent—before Honorata's reincarnation within her
peer_identity.honcho_notes: Voice: 'That is not the blue rose I want'—unwavering public standards. Courageous under lethal threat; held blade to herself to coerce father. Willing co-conspirator in Aghnar's infiltration plan. Deeply emotionally attached; merges psychic energy with Aghnar 'united forever.' Left mentally devastated after the battle. Genetically unique—Shabda-Oud target her womb for their breeding plan.
peer_identity.rationale: Separated from the Marmola Oda (different person) and from the Honorata-in-Oda records (vol09–10). In vol07–08, Oda operates with her own will: refuses suitors, holds a blade to herself to coerce her father, agrees to infiltrate the Shabda-Oud, tends Aghnar's wounds, merges psychic energy with him. She has a clear personal voice and agency. After vol08, Honorata's spirit supplants her identity. Keeping vol07–08 separate preserves Oda's distinct VOICE and TRAIT data for an authentic individual persona.

important_actions: Refused all suitors who did not bring the true blue rose (vol 7 p02–p04)
Accepted Aghnar's offer and verbally agreed to leave with him (vol 7 p05)
Held a blade to her chest or throat and forced her father to stand down under armed standoff (vol 7 p06)
Agreed to serve as Aghnar's feigned captive to infiltrate the Shabda-Oud lair (vol 7 p07)
Tended Aghnar's severe blood loss from his severed arm on the battlefield (vol 7 p24)
Merged psychic energy with Aghnar in a mind's-shadow union — described as making them 'united forever' — to help him survive the Elders' assault (vol 7 p25)
knowledge_boundaries: Left mentally devastated after the battle; condition regarding retained memories or cognition unknown at volume's close (vol 7 p27)
Her knowledge of the Shabda-Oud's plans (from having been inside their lair) is not explored before the mental injury occurs
relationships: character: Aghnar; type: beloved / partner / mind's-shadow union; notes: Agreed to join his plan; tended his wounds in battle; merged energy with him permanently in the mind's-shadow union (vol 7 p25)

character: Oda's Father (unnamed king); type: daughter — coerced relationship; notes: Father treated her as both kin and a claimed prospective wife; Oda explicitly rejects the marriage claim (vol 7 p06); forced him to release them by threatening suicide
character: Sama-Wajd; type: intended genetic progenitor; notes: Shabda-Oud believe her womb will produce the prophesied hermaphrodite Sama-Wajd

character: Honorata; type: uncertain — a woman who loved Oda more than anything; notes: Narration in vol 7 p11 mentions a woman who loved Oda more than anything; identity not fully resolved on that page alone
traits: Unwavering in her public demands — dismisses even the wealthiest and most powerful suitors who fail the blue-rose condition
Courageous under lethal threat; held a blade to herself to coerce her father
Submissive or compliant in her responses to Aghnar during their journey together
Described as beautiful and genetically unique — the Shabda-Oud consider her womb the key to their twelve-generation breeding plan
Deeply emotionally attached to Aghnar; merges her psychic energy with his in a permanent mind's-shadow union
voice_notes: Repeatedly: 'That is not the blue rose I want' — dismisses every substitute offering (vol 7 p02, p03)
Begs 'Aghnar' to save her during the forced Shabda-Oud ritual (vol 7 p17)
Responds affirmatively each time Aghnar describes their shared future (vol 7 p07, p08)
Alarmed rather than triumphant when the glowing cocoon appears after the final blast; asks what is happening (vol 7 p26)
witnessed_facts: Repeatedly witnessed suitors fail her blue-rose demand, including General Amagho's grotesque offering from a defeated emperor's remains (vol 7 p02)
Experienced Aghnar manifesting the true blue rose via psychic eye-beam (vol 7 p04)
Heard Aghnar's full tragic history and his plan to use her as a feigned captive (vol 7 p07)
Was subjected to the Shabda-Oud's forced reproductive ritual invoking Jejoh and Sama-Wajd (vol 7 p16, p17)
Was present and in danger during the main battle at the ice asteroid lair (vol 7 p19)
Witnessed Aghnar's arm severed and his stoic response (vol 7 p24)
Co-survived the Elders' psychic assault through the mind's-shadow union (vol 7 p25)

aliases: Oda-Honorata (used after Aghnar's accusation that Honorata inhabits her body)
appearances: description: Female; depicted in ornate biomechanical armor on cover with a forehead emblem or implant; later shown in pale ceremonial outfit; eventually appears reviving from a medical pod in a translucent sheet; source_refs: ['205_The_Metabarons_8_c01', '206_The_Metabarons_8_ic1', '219_The_Metabarons_8_p14']
important_actions: action: Won Aghnar's trust and agreed to help him seek revenge (recap); source_refs: ['206_The_Metabarons_8_ic1']
action: Joined Aghnar spiritually in final mental confrontation with elder witches (recap); source_refs: ['206_The_Metabarons_8_ic1']
action: Revived from catatonic state via Honorata's psycho-surgery with Tonto as assistant; source_refs: ['218_The_Metabarons_8_p13', '219_The_Metabarons_8_p14']
action: Gives birth to a bio-male son (later known as Steelhead); source_refs: ['222_The_Metabarons_8_p17']
action: Insists Aghnar should father a warrior heir; Aghnar disagrees; source_refs: ['221_The_Metabarons_8_p16']
action: Carries the near-fatally injured infant to Tonto for emergency grafting; source_refs: ['227_The_Metabarons_8_p22']
knowledge_boundaries: Her subjective consciousness during her catatonic/spiritually-dead state is unknown; Tonto states her soul had already departed
relationships: character: Aghnar; type: husband; notes: Deep mutual attachment; reunion after revival is wordless—only names spoken
character: Honorata; type: mother-in-law; accused usurper of her body; notes: Honorata performs psycho-surgery to revive her; Aghnar later accuses Honorata of having occupied her body via cloning
character: Tonto; type: surgical assistant; notes: Tonto assists Honorata in Oda's revival procedure
character: Steelhead; type: son (infant); notes: Conceives and gives birth to him; protects the infant even as a deadly conflict erupts
character: Shabda-Oud; type: captor (past); notes: Was delivered to the Shabda-Oud for breeding purposes as part of Aghnar's revenge scheme
traits: Brave enough to join Aghnar mentally in the final battle against the elder witches
Forceful and ideological about dynastic duty—strongly advocates producing a male warrior heir
Emotionally reduced to near-silence upon revival: can only say Aghnar's name
voice_notes: Insists child must be a son so the Metabaron line continues (p16)
Argues 'a good soul should not waste the chance to make his son the greatest warrior in the universe' (p16)
States the Castakas will not return to the warrior path, consistent with Aghnar's declaration (p13)
witnessed_facts: fact: Was chained to an altar on the witches' asteroid and participated in a ritual involving the god Jejoh (recap); source_refs: ['206_The_Metabarons_8_ic1']
fact: Joined Aghnar in the mental battle against the elder witches (recap); source_refs: ['206_The_Metabarons_8_ic1']
